newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot unionists call for end to division.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot unionists call for end to division.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot and Greek Cypriot trade unionists on Wednesday called for an end to the Mediterranean island's division after a rare three-day meeting that cut across the buffer zone splitting the two communities.
The meeting, which took place on both sides of the divided island, ended with a call for a solution to the long-standing dispute based on high-level agreements and United Nations resolutions.
"I think it is important that the unions of both communities got together to discuss their problems," Salih Usar, an executive committee member of the Turkish Cypriot union Dev-Is, told Reuters.

During the conference, which was financed by the European Union, delegates from 16 Greek and Turkish Cypriot trade unions discussed privatisation, movement of capital and labour and social policy in Europe.

Cyprus is due to start entry talks with the bloc next year but there is some question over whether the EU would be willing to accept the island before a solution was found to the split. The government in the south, where the Greek Cypriots live, is recognised internationally as the island's legitimate government.

The island has been divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the northern third after a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. Turkish Cypriots in 1983 declared a breakaway state only recognised by Turkey.
In a joint declaration issued after the conference, unions said they wanted to see a federated state in Cyprus with a unitary social security system and unified pay standards.
